records.source: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ· Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστής· αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: At that the time heard Herod the tetrarch the report of Jesus, \v 2 and he said to the servants of him, This is John the Baptist; he was raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are working in him.
pieces: Around that time, reports about Jesus reached Herod the tetrarch.
"This is John the Baptist," he told his courtiers. "He has been raised from the dead, and that is why he can do these mighty works."

L.1: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus,
L.2: and he said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him."

R.1: At that time Herod, the ruler of Galilee, heard what people were saying about Jesus.
R.2: He said to his servants, "This man is really John the Baptist! John has come back from the dead. That is why he has the power to do these miracles."

decisions.choice: Herod the tetrarch: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruler of Galilee and Perea
decisions.reason: Herod the Great had died (2:19). His son Antipas ruled Galilee and Perea under Rome from 4 BC to AD 39. A tetrarch was a ruler of part of a kingdom, below the rank of king.

decisions.choice: at that time: a loose link to the events just told
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the phrase to join stories without fixing a date (11:25; 12:1).

decisions.choice: he has been raised: Herod thinks John has come back to life, and that this explains Jesus's mighty works
alternatives: Herod means Jesus has the same spirit as John
decisions.reason: John did no miracles (compare John 10:41), so Herod explains the powers at work in Jesus by a return from the dead. His words also show a troubled conscience, as the story that follows explains. The passive points to God as the one who raises.

decisions.choice: servants: the officials and attendants of his court
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant; here it is the people who serve at Herod's court.

decisions.choice: mighty works (B); miracles (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the powers". Balanced and Readable say what the powers were: the miracles Jesus was doing (11:20-23).

decisions.choice: the ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: "Tetrarch" is unfamiliar; Readable says what Herod ruled that matters in Matthew's story.

records.heading: Herod and the death of John

records.source: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάννην ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ἔλεγεν γὰρ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν·
records.gloss: For Herod having seized John bound him and in prison put [him] because of Herodias the wife of Philip the brother of him; \v 4 was saying for John to him, Not it is lawful for you to have her.
pieces: Herod had earlier arrested John, put him in chains and locked him in prison. He did it for the sake of Herodias, who had been the wife of his brother Philip.
John had told Herod again and again, "The law does not allow you to have her."

L.3: For Herod, having seized John, had bound him and put [him] away in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother;
L.4: for John had been saying to him, "It is not lawful for you to have her."

R.3: Some time before this, Herod had arrested John. He tied him up and put him in prison. Herod did this because of Herodias. She had been the wife of Herod's brother Philip, but Herod had taken her as his own wife.
R.4: John kept telling Herod, "God's law says you must not marry her!"

decisions.choice: for: the story goes back to tell how John died
alternatives: the events follow Herod's words in time
decisions.reason: Matthew explains Herod's words (14:1-2) with a flashback that runs to 14:12. John's arrest was mentioned at 4:12 and his imprisonment at 11:2.

decisions.choice: Philip: the name Matthew gives Herodias's first husband, a half-brother of Antipas
alternatives: Philip the tetrarch, ruler of the lands northeast of the lake (Luke 3:1)
decisions.reason: The Jewish historian Josephus says Herodias was first married to a son of Herod the Great whom he calls Herod, and that Philip the tetrarch later married her daughter. Several sons of Herod the Great bore the family name Herod, so the first husband may also have been called Philip; Matthew follows Mark 6:17. The two accounts may name the same man differently, or one may be mistaken.

decisions.choice: the wife of Philip his brother, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wife of his brother, without the name, in a few manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few witnesses, including Codex Bezae and some Latin manuscripts, leave out the name Philip. The sense is the same: she was his brother's wife. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not lawful to have her: the law forbade marrying a brother's wife while the brother lived
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:16 and 20:21 forbid a man to take his brother's wife. Herodias had left her husband, who was still alive, to marry Antipas. The verb tense says John said it more than once.

decisions.choice: had earlier (B); some time before this (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the flashback plainly instead of beginning with "for".

decisions.choice: had taken her as his own wife; God's law says you must not marry her
alternatives: it is not lawful for you to have her
decisions.reason: Readable says what "have her" meant and whose law forbade it.

records.source: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
records.gloss: And wanting him to kill he feared the crowd, because as a prophet him they were holding.
pieces: He would have liked to put John to death, but he was afraid of the crowds, who looked on John as a prophet.

L.5: And though he wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him [to be] a prophet.

R.5: Herod wanted to kill John. But he was afraid of the people, because they thought John was a prophet from God.

decisions.choice: and wanting: though he wanted
decisions.reason: The participle sets Herod's wish against his fear: he wanted John dead, but fear of the people held him back.

decisions.choice: they held him as a prophet: the people believed God had sent John
alternatives: they thought him a teacher only
decisions.reason: Crowds went out to John at the Jordan (3:5), and Jesus himself called him a prophet and more (11:9). Matthew says the same of the crowds' view of John in 21:26.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John so that "him" is not taken for Herod or Jesus.

records.source: γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ, ὅθεν μετὰ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσηται.
records.gloss: Birthday now having come of Herod danced the daughter of Herodias in the midst and pleased Herod, \v 7 whereupon with an oath he promised to her to give whatever she might ask.
pieces: When Herod's birthday was being celebrated, Herodias's daughter danced in front of everyone. Herod was so delighted with her
that he swore to give her anything she asked for.

L.6: But when Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in the middle [of the guests] and pleased Herod,
L.7: so that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she might ask.

R.6: Then came Herod's birthday party. The daughter of Herodias danced in front of Herod and his guests. Herod liked her dancing very much.
R.7: So he made a promise and swore an oath to God. He said he would give her anything she asked for.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Herodias: her daughter by her first marriage, not named here
decisions.reason: Josephus names Herodias's daughter Salome. Matthew does not name her, and calls her a girl (14:11).

decisions.choice: birthday: the feast for Herod's birthday
alternatives: the anniversary of his coming to power
decisions.reason: The word means a birthday celebration. Mark 6:21 says Herod gave a banquet for his officials and the leading men of Galilee.

decisions.choice: with an oath: he swore by God to keep his promise
decisions.reason: An oath called on God as witness, and breaking it was a serious matter (5:33). Jesus had warned against swearing at all (5:34-37).

decisions.choice: whereupon: so that, as a result
decisions.reason: The word gives the result of Herod's delight in the dance.

decisions.choice: in the middle [of the guests]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the guests implied by the banquet (14:9).

decisions.choice: swore an oath to God
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom an oath was sworn.

records.source: ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς· Δός μοι, φησίν, ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.
records.gloss: And she having been urged on by the mother of her, Give me, she says, here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
pieces: Her mother told her what to say, and she answered, "Give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right here."

L.8: And she, having been prompted by her mother, says, "Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."

R.8: The girl's mother told her what to ask for. So the girl said to Herod, "Give me the head of John the Baptist on a big plate. Give it to me right here."

decisions.choice: having been prompted: urged on beforehand by her mother
alternatives: led forward by her mother onto the floor
decisions.reason: The verb means to push forward or put up to something. Mark 6:24 tells how the girl went out and asked her mother what to request.

decisions.choice: platter: a flat dish for serving food
decisions.reason: The word means a wide plate or dish, such as the dishes used at Herod's feast.

decisions.choice: here: at once, at the feast
decisions.reason: She wants the deed done now, before Herod can change his mind.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: the head of John the Baptist on a platter, right here
alternatives: here on a platter the head of John the Baptist
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the request first and the place last, which reads more naturally.

records.source: καὶ λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι, καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ·
records.gloss: And having been grieved the king because of the oaths and those reclining with [him] he commanded [it] to be given, \v 10 and having sent he beheaded John in the prison;
pieces: This grieved the king. Yet because of his oaths, and because of the guests at his table, he gave orders for her request to be granted.
He sent word to the prison, and there John was beheaded.

L.9: And the king was grieved, [but] because of the oaths and those reclining [at table] with [him], he commanded [it] to be given,
L.10: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.

R.9: The king was very sad. But he had sworn an oath, and his dinner guests had heard him. So he ordered his men to give the girl what she asked for.
R.10: He sent them to the prison, and they cut off John's head there.

decisions.choice: the king: Herod, called king loosely
decisions.reason: Antipas was a tetrarch (14:1), not a king, but people called him king (Mark 6:14). Years later he asked Rome for the title and lost his rule instead.

decisions.choice: grieved: sorry, distressed
decisions.reason: Herod regrets what he must do: he wanted John dead (14:5) but feared the people, and now he is trapped by his own oath.

decisions.choice: the oaths and those reclining with him: the oaths sworn before his dinner guests
alternatives: two separate reasons with no link
decisions.reason: Guests reclined on couches at a feast. To break an oath sworn in front of them would shame Herod. The plural "oaths" may mean he swore more than once.

decisions.choice: having sent, he beheaded John: he had John beheaded by others
alternatives: Herod did it with his own hand
decisions.reason: As often, the one who gives the order is said to do the deed. Mark 6:27 names an executioner.

decisions.choice: sent word to the prison (B); sent them to the prison (R)
alternatives: having sent, he beheaded John in the prison
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the order went and who carried it out.

decisions.choice: he had sworn an oath, and his dinner guests had heard him
alternatives: because of the oaths and the guests
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why the oath and the guests together held Herod to his word.

records.source: καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And was brought the head of him on a platter and was given to the girl, and she brought [it] to the mother of her.
pieces: Someone carried the head in on a platter and gave it to the girl, and she in turn brought it to her mother.

L.11: And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought [it] to her mother.

R.11: A man brought John's head on a plate and gave it to the girl. Then the girl took it to her mother.

decisions.choice: girl: a young girl
decisions.reason: The word is a diminutive used of a girl not yet grown, as of Jairus's daughter (9:24-25).

decisions.choice: she brought it to her mother: the request was the mother's from the start
decisions.reason: The story ends with Herodias, who wanted John silenced (14:3-4, 8).

decisions.choice: someone carried (B); a man brought (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the passive verb a subject; Matthew does not say who it was.

records.source: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And having come the disciples of him took the corpse and buried it, and having come they told Jesus.
pieces: Then John's disciples came for his body and buried it, and they went to tell Jesus what had happened.

L.12: And his disciples came and took the body and buried it, and they went and told Jesus.

R.12: John's followers came and took his body away, and they buried it. Then they went and told Jesus what had happened.

decisions.choice: his disciples: John's disciples
decisions.reason: John had disciples of his own (9:14; 11:2). They give their teacher the burial owed to the dead.

decisions.choice: body: a dead body, a corpse
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the dead.

decisions.choice: they told Jesus: John's death points ahead to Jesus's own
alternatives: a report with no further meaning
decisions.reason: John went before Jesus in his preaching (3:2; 4:17), in being handed over (4:12; 17:22), and now in death. Jesus later says that as they did to John, so the Son of Man will suffer (17:12).

decisions.choice: John's; what had happened
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose disciples these were and say what they reported.

records.source: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν· καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων.
records.gloss: Having heard now Jesus withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by himself; and having heard the crowds followed him on foot from the towns.
pieces: When Jesus heard the news, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and went off to a deserted place to be alone. But the crowds found out, and they came after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on foot from the towns.

L.13: Now when Jesus heard [it], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}; and when the crowds heard [of it], they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on foot from the towns.

R.13: Jesus heard what had happened to John. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left in a boat and went to a quiet place where no one lived. He wanted to be alone. But the crowds heard where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going. They left their towns and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, walking along the shore.

decisions.choice: having heard: Jesus heard of John's death, just reported to him
alternatives: he heard what Herod was saying about him (14:1-2)
decisions.reason: The verse follows the report of John's disciples (14:12), so the news of John's death is the nearest meaning. Because 14:3-12 looks back in time, some link it to Herod's words in 14:1-2 instead. Either way, Herod's attention is now on Jesus.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as Matthew says when danger is near
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the verb when Jesus moves away from a threat (2:14, 22; 4:12; 12:15).

decisions.choice: a deserted place: a lonely place with no village
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the wilderness. It was open country without towns, which is why the disciples worry about food (14:15).

decisions.choice: what had happened to John; walking along the shore
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus heard, as the meaning note explains, and that the crowds went by land around the lake while he went by boat. Matthew does not describe their route.

records.heading: Five loaves for a great crowd

records.source: καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And having gone out he saw a great crowd, and he was moved with compassion toward them and healed the sick of them.
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stepped ashore, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a large crowd. He felt deep pity for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed those among them who were sick.

L.14: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went ashore, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a great crowd, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had compassion on them and healed their sick.

R.14: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got out of the boat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed the people who were sick.

decisions.choice: having gone out: having come out of the boat
alternatives: having come out of the deserted place to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus came by boat (14:13), and the crowd had gone ahead on foot. He gets out and finds them already there.

decisions.choice: had compassion: was moved deep within
decisions.reason: As in 9:36, the verb speaks of strong feeling. Jesus had sought to be alone, but he does not send the crowd away.

decisions.choice: went ashore (L); stepped ashore (B); got out of the boat (R)
decisions.reason: Every level says what Jesus went out of, so that the reader does not picture him leaving the lonely place.

records.source: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν· ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ὄχλους, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα.
records.gloss: Evening now having come came to him the disciples saying, Deserted is the place and the hour already has passed; dismiss the crowds, that having gone into the villages they may buy for themselves food.
pieces: When evening came, the disciples went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "There is nothing out here, and the day is nearly over. Let the crowds go now, so they can find food to buy in the villages."

L.15: Now when evening came, the disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed. Send the crowds away, so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves."

R.15: Late in the afternoon, the followers came to Jesus. They said, "No one lives out here, and it is getting late. Send the people away. Then they can go to the villages and buy some food for themselves."

decisions.choice: evening: late in the afternoon, toward sunset
decisions.reason: The word covers the late part of the day. There is still time to reach the villages and buy food. A later "evening" in 14:23 is after dark.

decisions.choice: the hour has already passed: it is late in the day
decisions.reason: Both senses fit: the day is far gone, and the people have not eaten. The disciples' point is that there is little time left.

decisions.choice: dismiss: send away, let go
decisions.reason: The disciples ask Jesus to end the gathering so the people can look after themselves.

decisions.choice: late in the afternoon; the followers
decisions.reason: Readable gives the time of day in modern terms and says what disciples are.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν· δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.
records.gloss: But Jesus said to them, No need they have to go away; give them you to eat.
pieces: But Jesus told them, "They do not have to go away. Give them food yourselves."

L.16: But Jesus said to them, "They have no need to go away; you give them [something] to eat."

R.16: But Jesus said to them, "They do not need to leave. You feed them yourselves."

decisions.choice: you: the pronoun is stressed: you yourselves
decisions.reason: The Greek adds the pronoun for emphasis. Jesus puts the task on the disciples, who know they have almost nothing.

decisions.choice: give them to eat: perhaps an echo of Elisha feeding a hundred men
decisions.reason: Elisha told his servant to set a few loaves before a hundred men, and they ate and had some left over (2 Kings 4:42-44). Matthew does not cite the passage.

decisions.choice: yourselves
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable carry the stressed "you" with "yourselves".

records.source: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.
records.gloss: And they say to him, Not we have here except five loaves and two fish.
pieces: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have nothing here but five loaves and two fish."

L.17: And they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."

R.17: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All we have here are five small loaves of bread and two fish."

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat round loaves, each about a meal for one
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in small round flat loaves. Five of them would feed a few people. John 6:9 says they were barley loaves.

decisions.choice: fish: small fish, probably dried or salted
decisions.reason: Fish from the lake were salted or dried and eaten with bread.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: small loaves of bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of loaves these were.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Φέρετέ μοι ὧδε αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And he said, Bring to me here them.
pieces: He told them, "Bring them over here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.18: Jesus said, "Bring the bread and fish here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: bring them to me: the little they have is put in Jesus's hands
decisions.reason: The command moves the food from the disciples to Jesus before the crowd is fed.

decisions.choice: the bread and fish
decisions.reason: Readable names what is to be brought.

records.source: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ τοῦ χόρτου, λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.
records.gloss: And having commanded the crowds to recline on the grass, having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven he blessed, and having broken he gave to the disciples the loaves, and the disciples to the crowds.
pieces: He had the people sit down on the grass. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the five loaves and the two fish, raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes to heaven, and spoke the blessing. He broke the loaves and handed them to the disciples, and the disciples passed them to the crowds.

L.19: And having ordered the crowds to recline on the grass, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, [and] blessed, and having broken [them] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples [gave them] to the crowds.

R.19: Jesus told the people to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fish, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves into pieces and gave them to the followers. The followers gave the food to the people.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised God over the food
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing of God, who brings bread from the earth. The verb has no object here, so the praise is given to God.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the actions of the Last Supper
alternatives: ordinary actions at a meal with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the same four verbs when Jesus takes the bread at the Last Supper (26:26), and again at the second feeding (15:36).

decisions.choice: recline: lie down to eat, as at a meal
decisions.reason: People reclined to eat at a proper meal. Here the crowd is seated as guests at a meal Jesus provides.

decisions.choice: looked up to heaven: a gesture of prayer
alternatives: looked at the sky to judge the time
decisions.reason: People often prayed with eyes lifted toward heaven, God's dwelling (Psalm 123:1).

decisions.choice: sit down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the posture readers picture, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the food
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the blessing was spoken. Literal and Balanced keep the word "blessed".

records.source: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις.
records.gloss: And ate all and were satisfied, and they took up that being over and above of the fragments twelve baskets full.
pieces: Everyone ate and had enough. Then they collected what remained of the broken pieces, and it filled twelve baskets.

L.20: And all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up what was left over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.

R.20: All of the people ate as much as they wanted. After that, the followers gathered up the pieces of food that were left. They filled twelve baskets with them.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: were filled, had all they wanted
decisions.reason: The verb means to be fed until full. God gives his people bread until they are satisfied (Psalm 132:15).

decisions.choice: baskets: hand baskets of wicker
decisions.reason: This basket is the kind carried by hand. At the second feeding Matthew uses a different word for a larger basket (15:37; 16:9-10).

decisions.choice: twelve: one basket for each of the Twelve
alternatives: a symbol of the twelve tribes
decisions.reason: There is a basketful for each disciple who served the crowd. Some see a hint of the twelve tribes of Israel. The plain point is that more was left over than was there at the start.

decisions.choice: the followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who gathered the pieces. The disciples served the food (14:19) and would gather what was left; Matthew does not say so here.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.
records.gloss: Those then eating were men about five thousand besides women and children.
pieces: The men who ate numbered about 5,000, not counting women and children.

L.21: And those who ate were about 5,000 men, besides women and children.

R.21: About 5,000 men ate the food. Women and children ate too, but they were not counted.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word here means men as distinct from women and children, who are named next. The men were counted; the whole crowd was larger.

decisions.choice: besides women and children: they were there but not counted
alternatives: there were no women and children
decisions.reason: Matthew alone mentions them, here and at 15:38. Crowds were counted by the men.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals, as at Acts 4:4.

records.source: Καὶ εὐθέως ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν, ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους.
records.gloss: And immediately he compelled the disciples to get into a boat and to go before him to the other side, until he should dismiss the crowds.
pieces: Straight after this, Jesus insisted that the disciples get into the boat and go on before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} across the lake. Meanwhile {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would send the crowds home.

L.22: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the other side, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dismissed the crowds.

R.22: Right after that, Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to get into the boat. He made them go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the other side of the lake. He stayed behind to send the people home.

decisions.choice: compelled: made them go, insisted
alternatives: forced them against their will by threat
decisions.reason: The verb is strong. Matthew does not say why Jesus sent them off so firmly. John 6:15 tells that the crowd wanted to make Jesus king.

decisions.choice: until he dismissed the crowds: while he sent the crowds away
alternatives: they were to wait for him to dismiss them
decisions.reason: The disciples are to leave at once, and Jesus will send the crowds away himself.

decisions.choice: the other side: across the lake
decisions.reason: They arrive at Gennesaret (14:34).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Jesus comes to them across the water

records.source: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατ’ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι.
records.gloss: And having dismissed the crowds he went up into the mountain by himself to pray.
pieces: Once the crowds had gone, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} climbed up into the hills by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.

L.23: And having dismissed the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on the mountain by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.

R.23: After the people left, Jesus went up on a hill by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to pray.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country by the lake
decisions.reason: The word means a mountain or the hills. The hills rise steeply from the lake of Galilee. Matthew often places Jesus on a mountain (5:1; 15:29; 17:1; 28:16).

decisions.choice: by himself to pray: Jesus seeks God alone
decisions.reason: Jesus had taught his disciples to pray in secret (6:6). He goes alone again to pray in Gethsemane (26:36-44).

decisions.choice: into the hills (B); on a hill (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the hill country without suggesting a high peak.

records.source: ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ.
records.gloss: Evening now having come alone he was there.
pieces: Evening came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still there by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

L.23: And when evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was there alone.

R.23: When it got dark, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was there alone.

decisions.choice: evening: nightfall, after dark
decisions.reason: The same phrase as 14:15 marks a later point in the day. Hours have passed since the meal; the night is coming on.

decisions.choice: when it got dark
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this is later than the "evening" of 14:15.

records.source: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν, βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος.
records.gloss: And the boat already stadia many from the land was distant, being tormented by the waves, was for contrary the wind.
pieces: By then the boat was {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}} from shore, and the waves were pounding it, since the wind was blowing against them.

L.24: But the boat was already many stadia away from the land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against [it].

R.24: By this time the boat was far from land, {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}} out. The waves were beating hard against it, because the wind was blowing the wrong way.

decisions.choice: already many stadia away from the land, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: already in the middle of the sea, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "was already in the middle of the sea", as Mark 6:47 has it. The SBLGNT follows other early witnesses with "many stadia away from the land". Both mean the boat was far out on the lake. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: many stadia: a mile or more
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 600 feet (185 meters). Matthew gives no number. John 6:19 says the disciples had rowed twenty-five or thirty stadia, three miles or more.

decisions.choice: battered: tormented, harassed
decisions.reason: The verb means to torment, as of the suffering servant in 8:6. Here the waves torment the boat.

decisions.choice: the wind was against it: a headwind
decisions.reason: The wind blew against the direction they were trying to go, so they made little progress all night.

decisions.choice: {{units:a mile or more|many stadia}}
decisions.reason: The stadion means nothing to most readers, so Balanced and Readable give a distance in miles by default, and the units setting shows the original measure. Literal keeps the ancient unit.

records.source: τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν.
records.gloss: In fourth now watch of the night he came to them walking on the sea.
pieces: In the last watch of the night, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came out to them, walking on the water.

L.25: And in the fourth watch of the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to them, walking on the sea.

R.25: Sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning, Jesus came to them. He was walking on top of the water!

decisions.choice: the fourth watch of the night: from about three to six in the morning
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches. The disciples had struggled against the wind most of the night.

decisions.choice: walking on the sea: what Scripture says God alone does
decisions.reason: God alone treads on the waves of the sea (Job 9:8), and his path went through the sea at the exodus (Psalm 77:20). The disciples are far from land (14:24), so Matthew tells of a walk on the water itself.

decisions.choice: in the last watch of the night (B); sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning (R)
alternatives: in the fourth watch of the night
decisions.reason: Balanced says where the watch falls in the night; Readable gives the time in modern terms.

decisions.choice: the water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "water", since it is the walk on the surface that matters, and "sea" could suggest the open ocean. Literal keeps "sea".

records.source: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν.
records.gloss: And the disciples having seen him on the sea walking were troubled, saying, A ghost it is, and from the fear they cried out.
pieces: The disciples saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming across the water and were thrown into panic. "A ghost!" they cried, and they shouted out in terror.

L.26: And when the disciples saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the sea, they were terrified, saying, "It is a ghost!" And they cried out in fear.

R.26: The followers saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the water, and they were very scared. They said, "It is a ghost!" They screamed because they were so afraid.

decisions.choice: ghost: an apparition, a phantom
alternatives: the spirit of a dead person only
decisions.reason: The word means something seen that is not real flesh. The disciples think they see a spirit on the water at night.

decisions.choice: were terrified: were shaken, thrown into confusion
decisions.reason: The verb means to be stirred up or deeply disturbed, as Herod was in 2:3.

decisions.choice: coming across the water
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the wording after 14:25; the sense is the same.

records.source: εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι· μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
records.gloss: Immediately now spoke to them Jesus saying, Take courage, I am; not be afraid.
pieces: Jesus spoke to them at once: "Be brave! It is I. There is nothing to fear."

L.27: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Take courage; I am [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}]; do not be afraid."

R.27: Right away Jesus spoke to them. "Be brave!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is me, Jesus. Do not be afraid."

decisions.choice: I am: he tells them who he is, in words that echo the name God gave himself
decisions.reason: In ordinary speech the words mean "it is I". But God spoke of himself as "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in Isaiah God says "I am he" and tells his people not to fear (Isaiah 43:10; 51:12). Spoken by one who walks on the sea, the words may carry both senses; the plain sense is certain, the echo is likely but not sure.

decisions.choice: take courage: be bold, do not lose heart
decisions.reason: As in 9:2 and 9:22, Jesus speaks courage to people in need.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" tells them to stop the fear they already have (14:26). God and his messengers often say these words when they appear (Genesis 15:1; Isaiah 43:1).

decisions.choice: I am [he] (L); It is I (B); It is me, Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "I am". Literal brackets the "he" the plain sense needs; Balanced and Readable say the plain sense in everyday words. Readable adds the name so the plain sense is clear. The footnote gives the bare words, so the echo noted in the meaning decision stays visible.

records.source: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ εἶ, κέλευσόν με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα·
records.gloss: Answering now him Peter said, Lord, if you are, command me to come to you upon the waters.
pieces: Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, if it is really {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, give me the order to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} over the water."

L.28: And Peter answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Lord, if it is {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, command me to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the waters."

R.28: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, if it is really {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, tell me to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Tell me to walk on the water."

decisions.choice: Lord: an address of faith
decisions.reason: As in 8:25, the disciples call Jesus Lord when they turn to him for help and trust his power.

decisions.choice: if it is you: Peter wants to be sure, and asks for a word he can act on
alternatives: since it is you, with no doubt at all
decisions.reason: Peter answers Jesus's "it is I" by asking for a command. His words may hold some doubt, or simply eagerness to go to Jesus; the sense of the condition is open.

decisions.choice: command me to come: only Jesus's word can make it possible
decisions.reason: Peter does not ask to walk on his own; he asks Jesus to call him. He trusts the power of Jesus's command, as the centurion did (8:8).

decisions.choice: really
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "really" to show that Peter wants to be sure who it is.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἐλθέ.
records.gloss: And he said, Come.
pieces: "Come," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.

decisions.choice: come: the command Peter asked for
decisions.reason: Jesus gives the one-word command Peter asked for (14:28). It also echoes his call to follow him (4:19).

records.source: καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: And having gone down from the boat Peter walked upon the waters and came to Jesus.
pieces: So Peter climbed down out of the boat, stepped onto the water, and walked toward Jesus.

L.29: And going down from the boat, Peter walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.

R.29: So Peter got out of the boat. He walked on top of the water and went toward Jesus.

decisions.choice: and came toward Jesus, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: to come to Jesus, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "walked on the waters to come to Jesus", which says Peter set out to reach him. The SBLGNT reads "and came". Either way, Peter began to sink before he reached Jesus (14:30-31). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: came toward Jesus: went toward him, not reaching him
alternatives: came all the way to Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter begins to sink and Jesus has to reach out to him (14:30-31), so the verb means that he went toward Jesus.

decisions.choice: came toward (L); walked toward (B); went toward (R)
decisions.reason: Every level says "toward", as the meaning note explains.

records.source: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη, καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων· Κύριε, σῶσόν με.
records.gloss: Seeing now the wind strong he was afraid, and having begun to sink he cried out saying, Lord, save me.
pieces: But when he noticed how strong the wind was, fear took hold of him. He started to go under, and he shouted, "Lord, save me!"

L.30: But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, "Lord, save me!"

R.30: But Peter saw how strong the wind was, and he became afraid. He began to sink into the water. He shouted, "Lord, save me!"

decisions.choice: the strong wind, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the wind, without "strong", in some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read only "seeing the wind". Many others add "strong", which the SBLGNT prints. The sense is little changed: Peter looked at the wind and lost his nerve. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: seeing the wind he was afraid: he turned his eyes from Jesus to the danger
decisions.reason: Peter walked while he trusted Jesus's word. When he looked at the wind, fear took hold, and he began to sink. Jesus names the cause as doubt (14:31).

decisions.choice: Lord, save me: a cry for rescue in the words of prayer
decisions.reason: The cry echoes the Psalms' calls to God from deep waters (Psalm 69:2-3; 144:7), as at 8:25.

records.source: εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὀλιγόπιστε, εἰς τί ἐδίστασας;
records.gloss: Immediately now Jesus having stretched out the hand took hold of him and says to him, Of little faith, for why did you doubt?
pieces: Jesus at once put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and took hold of him. "You have so little faith," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him. "Why did you doubt?"

L.31: And immediately Jesus stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and took hold of him, and says to him, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"

R.31: Right away Jesus reached out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and caught Peter. Jesus said to him, "Your faith is so small! Why did you doubt?"

decisions.choice: of little faith: having real but weak trust
decisions.reason: As in 6:30 and 8:26, the word rebukes a disciple whose faith is real but gives way. Peter's faith carried him onto the water, and then failed.

decisions.choice: doubt: waver, be of two minds
decisions.reason: The verb means to hesitate between two ways. Matthew uses it again only in 28:17, of some who worshiped the risen Jesus.

decisions.choice: stretched out his hand and took hold of him: God's hand rescues from the waters
decisions.reason: A psalm asks God to reach down his hand from above and pull the psalmist out of deep waters (Psalm 144:7; compare 18:17). Jesus does what the psalm asks of God.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: You have so little faith (B); Your faith is so small (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the one-word address into a short statement, as at 6:30 and 8:26.

records.source: καὶ ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.
records.gloss: And having gone up they into the boat ceased the wind.
pieces: As soon as the two of them had climbed into the boat, the wind dropped.

L.32: And when they had gone up into the boat, the wind stopped.

R.32: Jesus and Peter got into the boat, and the wind stopped blowing.

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and Peter
decisions.reason: The other disciples were already in the boat; the two on the water climb in.

decisions.choice: ceased: grew tired, died down
decisions.reason: The verb means to grow weary or stop. The wind falls still once Jesus is in the boat, as in 8:26.

decisions.choice: the two of them (B); Jesus and Peter (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who climbed into the boat.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ.
records.gloss: Those then in the boat worshiped him saying, Truly of God Son you are.
pieces: Everyone in the boat fell down and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "You really are the Son of God!" they said.

L.33: And those in the boat worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Truly {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God."

R.33: Then everyone in the boat worshiped Jesus. They said, "It is true! You are the Son of God!"

decisions.choice: worshiped: bowed down before him in worship
alternatives: paid him respect as to a great man
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low before someone. Matthew uses it of the magi (2:11) and of worship due to God alone (4:10). After what they have seen, the disciples give Jesus the honor that belongs to God.

decisions.choice: Truly you are the Son of God: the first time the disciples confess Jesus as God's Son
alternatives: a son of God, a godlike man
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, but the title is the one God spoke at Jesus's baptism (3:17) and the tempter and demons used (4:3, 6; 8:29). Here the disciples say it in worship. Peter will confess it again (16:16), and a centurion at the cross (27:54).

decisions.choice: those in the boat: the disciples, perhaps with others
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "those in the boat". The disciples are meant, and no one else is mentioned.

decisions.choice: [the] Son of God
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the article the Greek leaves out, as at 4:3.

records.source: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρέτ.
records.gloss: And having crossed over they came to the land into Gennesaret.
pieces: After crossing the lake, they came ashore at Gennesaret.

L.34: And having crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.

R.34: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed the lake and landed at a place called Gennesaret.

decisions.choice: Gennesaret: a fertile plain on the northwest shore of the lake of Galilee
alternatives: a town on the eastern shore
decisions.reason: The plain of Gennesaret lay south of Capernaum. The lake itself was sometimes called by the same name (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; a place called
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Readable says who crossed and that Gennesaret is a place.

records.heading: Healing at Gennesaret

records.source: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην, καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ· καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν.
records.gloss: And having recognized him the men of the place that sent into all the surrounding region that and brought to him all those sick being, \v 36 and they were begging him that only they might touch the fringe of the garment of him; and as many as touched were made completely well.
pieces: The people of that place knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and they sent messengers all through the region around. They brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was ill
and pleaded to be allowed simply to touch the tassel of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. Every one of them who touched it was fully healed.

L.35: And when the {{gender:people|men}} of that place recognized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they sent into all that surrounding region and brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all who were sick,
L.36: and they kept begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that they might only touch the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment; and as many as touched [it] were made completely well.

R.35: The people who lived there knew who Jesus was. So they sent messages to all the places around. People brought everyone who was sick to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.36: They begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to let the sick people touch just the edge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes. And every sick person who touched it was healed.

decisions.choice: the men of that place: the people who lived there
decisions.reason: "The men of" a place is a common way of naming its people, as "the men of Nineveh" in 12:41.

decisions.choice: the fringe of his garment: the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38-39; Deuteronomy 22:12). The people hope for what the woman found in 9:20-22. The word can also mean simply the edge.

decisions.choice: were made completely well: brought safely through, fully healed
decisions.reason: The verb is a strengthened form of the word for "save" used in 9:21-22. It means a complete healing.

decisions.choice: were begging: kept begging, one after another
decisions.reason: The tense pictures request after request as the sick were brought.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: Literal uses the gender setting for the general "men of that place", as at 12:41. Balanced and Readable say "people", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: fringe (L); tassel (B); edge (R)
decisions.reason: As at 9:20: Literal keeps "fringe", Balanced names the tassel, and Readable uses the simpler "edge".
